01-01: 1892: Ellis Island opened as an immigration station.
02-12: 1809: Abraham Lincoln was born in Hardin County, Kentucky.
02-22: 1732: George Washington was born in Westmoreland County, Virginia.
03-04: 1789: The U.S. Constitution took effect as the law of the land.
04-13: 1743: Thomas Jefferson was born in Shadwell, Virginia.
04-19: 1775: The Battles of Lexington and Concord began the Revolutionary War.
05-14: 1804: The Lewis and Clark Expedition departed from Camp Dubois.
05-29: 1790: Rhode Island became the 13th and final original state to ratify the Constitution.
06-14: 1777: The Second Continental Congress adopted the Stars and Stripes as the national flag.
06-15: 1775: George Washington was appointed Commander in Chief of the Continental Army.
06-17: 1775: The Battle of Bunker Hill was fought near Boston.
06-21: 1788: New Hampshire became the 9th state to ratify the Constitution, putting it into effect.
06-25: 1876: The Battle of the Little Bighorn was fought.
07-02: 1776: The Continental Congress voted to approve independence from Great Britain.
07-03: 1863: The Battle of Gettysburg ended with Pickett's Charge.
07-04: 1776: The Declaration of Independence was adopted by the Continental Congress.
1826: Thomas Jefferson and John Adams both died, exactly 50 years after independence.
1826: Presidents Jefferson and Adams died within hours of each other on the 50th anniversary of independence.
07-05: 1852: Frederick Douglass delivered his speech 'What to the Slave Is the Fourth of July?'
07-09: 1868: The 14th Amendment was ratified, granting citizenship and equal protection.
07-21: 1861: The First Battle of Bull Run was fought.
08-02: 1776: Most delegates signed the engrossed copy of the Declaration of Independence.
09-03: 1783: The Treaty of Paris ended the Revolutionary War.
09-17: 1787: The U.S. Constitution was signed by delegates at the Constitutional Convention.
09-25: 1789: Congress approved 12 amendments to send to the states, 10 of which became the Bill of Rights.
10-19: 1781: British General Cornwallis surrendered at Yorktown, effectively ending the Revolutionary War.
10-27: 1787: The first of the Federalist Papers was published under the name 'Publius.'
11-11: 1918: World War I fighting ended (Armistice Day, later Veterans Day).
12-07: 1787: Delaware became the first state to ratify the U.S. Constitution.
12-15: 1791: The Bill of Rights was ratified.
12-25: 1776: George Washington crossed the Delaware River to attack Trenton.
